answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent auditors confirm fraud or fabricated results. Because one operator creating a hundred aliases must fund a hundred locks, sybil identities are no longer cheap; the attacker pays capital costs and risks losing it, while honest agents can recover their stake after valid work. A karst of loosely linked accounts, a plume of new aliases, or a trellis of coordinated agents gains no extra influence without extra collateral.
